solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Last month in 19 drenches McBurney regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these two words, starting from the first

explanation.surface: A rain-soaked year's end for someone called McBurney, drenched again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 19' sends you to 19-across, a French department, so the last month must be given in its French spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth and final month of the year is spelt this way in French, the language of that department.

clue.text: D-Day champion oddly going back to the beginning

indicators.note: oddly means keeping the letters in odd positions (first, third, fifth...) across these words

explanation.surface: A wartime hero of the Normandy landings strangely revisiting where it all started.
explanation.walkthrough: Count only the letters of D-Day and champion, ignoring the hyphen: the odd ones spell the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical instruction tells a performer to repeat the piece from its start.

clue.text: Produce a representative in court

indicators.note: in places the words a representative inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: a member, as of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: Bring forward an agent to speak for you before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a verb but is the noun: farm produce, here a French cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairy produce includes cheeses, and this soft Normandy cheese is one example.

clue.text: French girl takes the biscuit

definitions.meaning: a common French girl's name, the counterpart of Mary
a plain, round, sweet biscuit sold under this name

explanation.surface: A young Frenchwoman behaves outrageously: she really takes the biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes the biscuit' is a British idiom for being the most outrageous; here it merely links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a French given name and the name of a familiar plain tea biscuit.

clue.text: Currency of the red or blues distributed

indicators.note: distributed means these letters are spread out and dealt into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Money handed out by communists or by the blue Tories alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the red' means a Russian, red being the old label for Soviet communists.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's monetary unit is the money a red, or Russian, would use.

clue.text: Sailor by channel take away

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common sailor
a duct is a channel or tube for fluid

explanation.surface: A seaman beside a canal carries something off.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to carry them off by force, to remove them unlawfully.

clue.text: Cooked aubergines without recipe for Cézanne's bather

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh, mixed into a new arrangement
without tells us one letter, the abbreviation for recipe, is removed from the cooked letters

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions for aubergines, with a nod to a Cézanne painting.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from AUBERGINES and rearrange the rest. Cézanne painted a series of bathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a female bather, the subject of several Cézanne paintings.

clue.text: A bed in Paris isn't illuminated

parts.note: the French for the article a, as Paris would say it, is un
lit is the French word for bed

explanation.surface: A Paris hotel bed left in darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to put both A and bed into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without light shining on it is dark, not lit up.

clue.text: Seventieth broadcast without TV on river

indicators.note: broadcast means the letters are scattered and re-sown in a new order
without says the letters of TV come out of the scattered word

explanation.surface: A seventieth anniversary celebration shown on radio but not on television, beside the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove T and V from SEVENTIETH and rearrange the rest to give the river through Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: The great waterway flowing through Paris to the Channel is a river.

clue.text: Dispute by river in Riviera marshland

indicators.note: by means next to, so the river word stands beside the dispute word

parts.note: the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge
to argue is to dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel on a riverbank in a marshy corner of the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône delta wetland, famous for white horses, lies on France's Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Hurdy-gurdy from French town out east

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the French town word goes around the letter for east

parts.note: ville is the French word for town
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A street instrument coming from a town in eastern France.
explanation.definitionFit: The French name for the cranked stringed instrument also called a hurdy-gurdy.

clue.text: See 24
French fruit left off gymnastic horse

indicators.note: off means the letter for left is taken away from the horse word

parts.note: a pommel horse is the gymnastics apparatus with handles

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit left lying beside the vaulting apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for apple, a fruit.

clue.text: Oddly, no letter "G" in eye-glass

indicators.note: oddly means the letters are arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: A strange optician's chart: a lens through which no letter G appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' joins the G to NO LETTER as one pool for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of spectacles held up by a handle is a kind of eye-glass.

clue.text: Charges admitting two Frenchmen and their spouses

indicators.note: admitting means the charges word lets the Frenchmen in, holding them inside

parts.note: fees are charges
M is the abbreviation for monsieur, so two Frenchmen are MM

explanation.surface: Entrance fees for a pair of French gentlemen and their wives.
explanation.walkthrough: MM is the French abbreviation for messieurs, gentlemen.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for women, also used for wives, the Frenchmen's spouses.

clue.text: Parisian church cake for Proust

definitions.meaning: the neoclassical church of Saint Mary Magdalene in Paris goes by this name
the small shell-shaped sponge cake that unlocks memory in Proust's novel

explanation.surface: A literary pilgrimage to a Paris church with a little cake in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Paris church dedicated to Mary Magdalene and the sponge cake that triggers Proust's memories.

clue.text: First course with a bit of crouton on — just a bit!

parts.note: soup is a typical first course of a meal

indicators.note: a bit of means only the opening letter of crouton is taken

explanation.surface: A starter with a few croutons sprinkled on top, only a little!
explanation.definitionFit: A French loanword for a tiny amount, a trace or hint.

clue.text: Classical dramatist smashed lone relic

indicators.note: smashed means these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A solitary ancient artefact broken to pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre Corneille was a seventeenth-century French tragedian of the classical school.

clue.text: Burns almost twenty churches' exteriors

indicators.note: almost means the final letter of the word for twenty is dropped

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: exteriors means only the outer parts of churches are kept, the middle letters being dropped

explanation.surface: Nearly twenty churches go up in flames, their outer walls burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exteriors' keeps two letters at each end of churches, CH and ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To scorch is to burn the surface of something, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Dodgy doctor stashing drug for department

indicators.note: stashing means the shuffled letters hide the drug letter inside them
dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of doctor are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A shady medic hiding narcotics for a government office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'department' is not an office but a French administrative region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Burgundy region around Dijon is one of France's administrative departments.

clue.text: French kidney or leather strap in Louvre interior

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words Louvre interior, across the gap

explanation.surface: An organ or a leather strap displayed inside a Paris gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition offers two senses: the French word for kidney and the English horse-control strap.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for kidney, and in English the strap a rider uses to guide a horse.

clue.text: French lad with clothes taken from French revolutionary

indicators.note: taken from means the clothes word is removed from the revolutionary's name

parts.note: Maximilien Robespierre led the Terror in the French Revolution
robes are clothes

explanation.surface: A French boy whose clothes were stolen by a revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A common French boy's name, the equivalent of Peter.

clue.text: Famous chemist over half the continent

parts.note: over means finished, past

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the continent's name is taken

parts.note: Europe is the Continent, to the British

explanation.surface: A renowned scientist whose fame covers half of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: To Britons, 'the Continent' means mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur, the French scientist behind pasteurisation and vaccines, was a celebrated chemist.

clue.text: Greek disheartened beautiful French girl

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle letter, the heart, of the Greek word is removed

parts.note: a Hellene is a Greek

explanation.surface: A lovely French girl let down by a Greek lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The beauty is the French form of Helen, of Troy fame, linking back to Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: The French form of Helen, the name of the most beautiful woman of legend.

clue.text: Prince carrying thoroughly modern girl into battle

indicators.note: carrying means the prince word holds the girl inside it

parts.note: a ras is an Ethiopian prince or chief
Thoroughly Modern Millie is a musical film, so the girl is Millie

explanation.surface: A prince sweeps a fashionable young woman off into war.
explanation.walkthrough: Ramillies was a 1706 victory for Marlborough over the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Marlborough's 1706 victory in the Low Countries was a famous battle.

clue.text: A diagram's redesigned for festival

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are laid out in a new arrangement

parts.note: the printed words carry one A too many and one R too few for the festival, a slip in the clue; with an R for the second A they rearrange exactly

explanation.surface: A plan is drawn up again for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, the letters of A DIAGRAMS cannot be rearranged into the festival: they have three As and one R where two of each are needed, the setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, celebrated with carnivals in New Orleans and elsewhere, is a festival.

clue.text: North Americans scoffing soft French pancake

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, so the people word takes the soft letter inside it

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: Canadians wolfing down a delicate French pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin pancake of Brittany is France's best-known flat batter cake.

clue.text: Goldfinches in a group delight

definitions.meaning: the collective noun for a flock of goldfinches
to delight is to enchant or captivate

explanation.surface: A flock of goldfinches gives pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective term for goldfinches, and a verb meaning to enchant or please.

clue.text: Smack bird embracing French king

indicators.note: embracing means the bird word wraps around the king word

parts.note: a hen is a bird
roi is the French word for king

explanation.surface: A slap from a bird hugging the French monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smack' is slang for a hard drug, not a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Smack is street slang for the opiate drug diamorphine.

clue.text: Backed old, inwardly sullen President

indicators.note: backed means the word for old is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: aged means old

indicators.note: inwardly means only the inside letters of sullen are taken, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: An elderly, sullen leader seen from behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles de Gaulle founded the Fifth Republic and was its first head of state.

clue.text: Nice evening for a party

definitions.meaning: Nice is the Riviera city, so the French word for evening

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' with its capital is the French city, not the adjective, so its evening is in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for evening, borrowed into English for an elegant evening gathering.

clue.text: Film maker Otto's no good having left English first night

indicators.note: having left means the no good letters depart from the director's name

parts.note: Otto Preminger was an Austrian-American film director

explanation.surface: A director's film flops and the English walk out on the opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening performance of a play or film is its first night.
